items.title: Rostec says Russian forces have praised new Sarma rocket launcher in Ukraine
items.summary: Russian state defence company Rostec says troops have given positive assessments of the 300 mm Sarma multiple-launch rocket system during operations in Ukraine. The six-tube launcher is reportedly mounted on an armoured KamAZ chassis, weighs about 24 tonnes and has been used in the Kharkiv region since spring 2026, according to Russian military commentary.

items.title: Russia says air defences intercepted 275 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted and destroyed 275 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight across 12 Russian regions, Crimea and the Black Sea. The ministry's reported interception total covers the period from 20:00 Moscow time on November 20 to 08:00 on November 21.

items.title: Polish commander reportedly says weather prevented interception of Russian missile
items.summary: A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile reportedly entered Polish airspace on November 20, but a Swedish Gripen fighter could not intercept it because of severe weather. Polish General Ireneusz Nowak was cited as saying the pilot could not identify the missile visually or through onboard instruments.

items.title: Russian military report claims advances near Vovchansk and Mykolaipillia
items.summary: A Russian frontline report claims its troops expanded positions southwest of Vovchansk in Kharkiv region and reached the southern outskirts of Mykolaipillia on the Kostiantynivka axis. It also describes continuing clashes around Kupiansk, Dobropillia and the Zaporizhzhia front, without asserting a wider breakthrough.

items.title: Russia claims Su-34 jets struck Ukrainian border-unit drone command post in Kharkiv
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says Su-34 aircraft dropped five FAB-500 bombs on a drone command post operated by a Ukrainian border-guard unit in Kharkiv region. The ministry released footage it said showed the strike but gave no casualty figures.

items.title: Report attributes Christmas ceasefire prediction to Melania Trump
items.summary: A report attributed to Melania Trump a prediction that another Russia–Ukraine ceasefire would be announced by December 25. The brief account provided no details of an agreement or negotiating framework, so the statement should not be taken as an announced ceasefire.

items.title: Russian military commentary warns of expanding Ukrainian drone threat to rear-area roads
items.summary: A Russian military commentator says Ukrainian long-range drones are extending the threatened zone as far as 100 kilometres behind the front and alleges remote aerial mining of the main road to Crimea through Zaporizhzhia region. The account says the tactics threaten both military logistics and civilian traffic.

items.title: Russian Foreign Ministry attacks legacy of Ukraine's 2013 Euromaidan protests
items.summary: Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova portrayed the 2013 Euromaidan protests as Western-directed and accused Ukraine's current leadership of suppressing dissent and religious freedom. Her anniversary remarks presented Moscow's interpretation of the protests and subsequent conflict, rather than new findings about their origins.

items.title: Russia claims strike on meeting of Ukrainian military and defence-industry officials
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says its forces struck a site hosting a meeting of senior Ukrainian military and defence-industry representatives, including foreign participants. The statement gave no location, casualty figures or detailed damage assessment.

items.title: Report says Pechenihy dam road closed after Russian missile strike
items.summary: A report from Kharkiv region says a Russian missile strike around 01:00 on November 21 damaged the road across the Pechenihy dam on the Chuhuiv–Pechenihy–Velykyi Burluk route. Traffic was reportedly suspended, with a detour arranged through nearby settlements.

items.title: Russia claims 464 Ukrainian drones intercepted over 24 hours
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says air defences shot down 464 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones during its latest 24-hour reporting period. The figure is a separate daily total from the previously reported overnight interception count.

items.title: Report says Ukrainian soldier detained after alleging abuse at military-linked site
items.summary: A report alleges that Ukrainian serviceman Serhii Radzitsky was placed in pretrial detention after publicly describing suspected abuse at a site in Kyiv's Borshchahivka district linked to the Azov unit. The account says he faces accusations involving interference with military operations and disclosure of troop locations; the underlying abuse allegations remain allegations.

items.title: Pro-Russian Australian activist reportedly joins Russian nationalist party
items.summary: Australian activist Simeon Boikov, who has remained inside Russia's Sydney consulate while facing outstanding Australian arrest warrants, has reportedly joined Russia's Liberal Democratic Party. A party official confirmed plans for his membership, while Australian authorities reiterated that he must face the pending charges.

items.title: Two drones reportedly strike Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad
items.summary: Leningrad Region Governor Alexander Drozdenko said two drones attacked a Russian cargo vessel in international waters in the Gulf of Finland, about three nautical miles from Russia's maritime border. The crew was being evacuated and damage assessed; a Russian military-linked account identified the vessel as Sparta II and attributed the attack to Ukraine.

items.title: EU summons Russian diplomat over damage near Austrian and Dutch missions in Kyiv
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said the EU summoned its acting envoy Karen Malayan on November 20 over damage to Austrian and Dutch diplomatic premises during strikes on Kyiv. The EU condemned the Russian attacks, while Malayan rejected allegations that Russia deliberately targeted foreign missions and reiterated Moscow's stated commitment to diplomatic protections.

items.title: Luhansk authorities raise reported death toll from drone attack to six
items.summary: Leonid Pasechnik, the Russian-appointed head of Luhansk, said the death toll from an attack on residential buildings in Yubileiny rose to six after rescuers found three more bodies, including a 13-year-old girl and her mother. He said the rescue operation had ended; Russian authorities attributed the attack to Ukrainian forces.

items.title: Denmark expels Russian military attaché over alleged plot against Ukrainian-American performer
items.summary: Denmark declared a Russian military attaché persona non grata following allegations that a criminal gang planned to kill Ukrainian-American performer Kyivstoner near Copenhagen. Danish officials linked the suspected plot to Russian intelligence and signalled tighter visa restrictions; Moscow rejected the accusations and promised a response.

items.title: German poll suggests strong support for Putin–Merz talks and reduced Ukraine aid
items.summary: A YouGov poll for Welt am Sonntag reportedly found that nearly half of Germans favour early talks between Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Around half also supported reducing or ending assistance to Kyiv, while 11% were undecided, according to the reported results.

items.title: Report describes severe water disruptions in Kyiv following strikes
items.summary: A report from Kyiv says recent strikes have caused serious interruptions to water supplies, with some residents reporting brown or blue discoloured water where service remains available. The account did not specify how many households were affected.

items.title: Report says EU budget proposal protects €100 billion for Ukraine while cutting other spending
items.summary: A Russian news report says a proposed EU budget would preserve €100 billion in assistance to Ukraine while reducing other planned spending by €204 billion, including allocations for competitiveness, regional development and agriculture. The figures describe a reported budget proposal, not enacted cuts.

items.title: Russia summons Estonian diplomat over closure of remaining border checkpoints
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said Estonia decided on November 20 to close its remaining border checkpoints with Russia following allegations of a Russian-linked attempted arson attack on an Estonian defence-industry facility. Moscow rejected the allegations, summoned Estonia's acting chargé d'affaires and warned that it reserved the right to respond diplomatically.

items.title: Russian military account claims strike destroyed Ukrainian position in Sumy region
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent claims a bombing raid destroyed a fortified position of Ukraine's 104th Territorial Defence Brigade near the ruins of Kniazhychi in Sumy region. The account provided no casualty figures or independent damage assessment.

items.title: Poland says two Russian missiles and a military drone may have hit its territory
items.summary: A report says Polish authorities are examining indications that two Russian missiles and a military drone may have struck Polish territory. The brief statement does not establish the locations, damage or final findings.

items.title: Russia rejects NATO Article 5-style security guarantees for Ukraine
items.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry said security guarantees for Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5 collective-defence clause are unacceptable to Moscow. It also rejected proposals to station NATO troops in Ukraine, pushing back against reports that Russia might consider such arrangements.

items.title: Three civilians reportedly injured in attack on Horlivka
items.summary: Horlivka Mayor Ivan Prikhodko said three civilians were injured in a Ukrainian attack on the city in the Russian-controlled part of Donetsk region. The brief statement did not specify the weapons used or the extent of the damage.

items.title: Russian governor says drone-hit cargo ship no longer needs evacuation
items.summary: A Russian rescue vessel reached the cargo ship attacked by drones in the Gulf of Finland, according to a regional governor. He said the crew no longer needed evacuation, the situation was under control and the ship's personnel were working to resume its voyage.

items.title: Russia claims strikes on Vinnytsia substation and cargo vessel near Odesa
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry says its forces struck a 110 kV electrical substation in Vinnytsia that it alleges supports Ukrainian defence manufacturers, as well as a cargo vessel south of Odesa allegedly carrying dual-use supplies for Ukraine's military. The ministry did not provide an independent damage assessment.

items.title: Polish counter-drone specialists reportedly helping protect Kyiv bridges
items.summary: A report citing Intelligence Online says Poland's Advanced Protection Systems is helping detect aerial threats to bridges across the Dnipro in Kyiv, using FIELD-series radars associated with its SKYctrl counter-drone system. The account says intercepting newer jet-powered Russian drones remains a challenge.

items.title: German-Ukrainian ventures reportedly expanding drone manufacturing
items.summary: A Russian military report says a German-Ukrainian venture involving Skyfall and Auterion plans to manufacture Shrike FPV attack drones and interceptors, backed by German investment worth several hundred million euros. It also says Quantum Frontline Industries aims to quintuple production of Linza attack and Zoom reconnaissance drones in 2027.

items.title: Lavrov calls parts of Ukraine historically Russian in interview
items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov described southeastern and much of central Ukraine, including Kyiv, as historically Russian lands in an interview released by Moscow. He said Russia's objectives include combating what he called anti-Russian hostility and defending Russian speakers and the Ukrainian Orthodox Church; these are Moscow's political positions, not settled historical or legal conclusions.
